page: Microsoft Azure F8amds_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs, operating with a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 945 GB NVMe SSD and is premium storage capable. No GPU accelerators are present on this server type.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU execution, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10% tier. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core CPU, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and PassMark CPU scores, falls within the average middle 50% range. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, along with PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations, also register average performance. For language model workloads, the server achieves top 10% text generation speeds with small 135M models, but drops to the bottom 10% for prompt processing on large 70B models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the F8amds_v7 offers a high density of memory and local NVMe SSD storage relative to its 8 vCPUs. This resource density makes it a balanced option for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity without the need to scale up to higher vCPU tiers. However, a key tradeoff is the average multi-core scaling and the significant performance drop observed during large-scale LLM processing, indicating that compute-heavy multi-threaded tasks or large AI models may hit resource bottlenecks.

The hardware profile and benchmark results indicate that this server is suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, and single-threaded processing tasks. The combination of 64.0 GB of RAM and 945 GB of local NVMe SSD storage supports database hosting, caching layers, and web serving workloads. It is also capable of handling lightweight machine learning inference for small models, though it is not designed for large-scale model execution.
